Nepal Wire's take: A former Chief Justice was arrested at his home on Sunday and nobody in authority has said why. Lawmakers filed 21 allegations against Cholendra Shumsher Rana in 2022 and Parliament never voted. The Supreme Court closed that file on September 9. Now police hold a complaint they will not describe. The Constitution gives them 24 hours to put him before a judge. That deadline is the first real test of this arrest.

────────────────────────
THE STORY
────────────────────────

Former Chief Justice Cholendra Rana Arrested From Kathmandu Home, Complaint Undisclosed

Police gave no charge and have not linked the arrest to his four year impeachment saga, which the Supreme Court closed just weeks earlier.

Police arrested former Chief Justice Cholendra Shumsher Rana from his home in Maharajgunj overnight into Sunday, according to the Kathmandu Post, Ratopati, OnlineKhabar, Nagarik and several other outlets. Nepali outlets including Ratopati, OnlineKhabar and Nagarik refer to him as Cholendra Shumsher Jabra. A team from the Kathmandu Valley Crime Investigation Office in Teku carried out the arrest, a senior police source told multiple outlets.

Police have not said what the complaint against Rana alleges. DC Nepal and Khabarhub both reported that officers gave no details of the case that triggered the arrest. Desh Sanchar and Nepal Press carried the same line. Ratopati and Desh Sanchar reported that a complaint was filed at the Valley Crime Investigation Office, but its contents remain undisclosed.

His nearly four year term as Chief Justice ended in a public storm over corruption allegations that Parliament never resolved. Now the courts he once led will decide whether police can keep holding him.

A term that ended in crisis

Rana was sworn in as Chief Justice in early January 2019, succeeding Om Prakash Mishra, according to the Kathmandu Post. His term became engulfed in controversy from October 2021, when fellow Supreme Court justices and the Nepal Bar Association accused him of seeking political favors and interfering in judicial appointments, the Kathmandu Post reported.

On February 13, 2022, 98 lawmakers from the ruling coalition registered an impeachment motion against him in Parliament, citing 21 separate allegations of misconduct and corruption, the Kathmandu Post reported at the time. The motion automatically suspended him from office. Parliament never voted on it before the House term expired later that year. Rana retired in December 2022 with the case still unresolved.

The impeachment sat in legal limbo for more than four years. On September 9 this year, the Supreme Court's Constitutional Bench ruled that the motion had lost its purpose and dismissed a related petition, the Kathmandu Post reported. That decision closed the impeachment saga just over two weeks before Sunday's arrest. No outlet has reported any connection between that ruling and the arrest.

What happens next

No charge sheet has been made public. None of the reports cited here mention his release. No outlet has reported him appearing before a court or facing a formal charge. Article 20 of the Constitution of Nepal requires that anyone arrested be brought before a judge within 24 hours, not counting travel time, so the next test comes fast. By Monday, police must bring him before a judge or let him go.

Until they do, every detail of the arrest itself rests on the same unnamed police sources cited by Ratopati, OnlineKhabar, Nagarik, DC Nepal, Nepal Press and Khabarhub. None of the reports say whether the new complaint is linked to the corruption allegations that shadowed his tenure, or to something else entirely. Readers should treat any link between the 2022 impeachment claims and this new complaint as unconfirmed until police or a court record says otherwise.

────────────────────────

Sources: Kathmandu Post, Ratopati, OnlineKhabar, Nagarik News, DC Nepal, Nepal Press, Khabarhub (English), Desh Sanchar (English), Constitution of Nepal 2015, Article 20(3)

Every source, with links: https://inquisitive013.github.io/nepal-news-rss/articles/former-chief-justice-cholendra-rana-arrested/

पूर्वप्रधानन्यायाधीश जबरा घरबाटै पक्राउ, उजुरी सार्वजनिक भएन

मुलुकको प्रधानन्यायाधीश भइसकेका व्यक्ति आफ्नै घरबाट पक्राउ परे।
प्रहरी भने कारण बताउन अझै तयार छैन।

प्रहरीले पूर्वप्रधानन्यायाधीश चोलेन्द्रशमशेर जबरालाई आइतबार काठमाडौंको महाराजगञ्जस्थित निवासबाट पक्राउ गरेको छ। टेकुस्थित काठमाडौं उपत्यका अपराध अनुसन्धान कार्यालयको टोलीले पक्राउ गरेको प्रहरीका एक उच्च स्रोतले सञ्चारमाध्यमलाई बताएका छन्।

पक्राउको आधार बनेको उजुरीमा के लेखिएको छ भन्ने प्रहरीले अहिलेसम्म खुलाएको छैन। रातोपाटी र देश सञ्चारका अनुसार अपराध अनुसन्धान कार्यालयमा एउटा उजुरी दर्ता भएको छ। तर त्यसको विवरण सार्वजनिक भएको छैन।

२०२२ मा ९८ सांसदले जबराविरुद्ध २१ वटा आरोप राखी महाभियोगको प्रस्ताव दर्ता गरेका थिए। संसदले त्यसमाथि कहिल्यै मतदान गरेन र उनी उही वर्ष अवकाशमा गए। सर्वोच्च अदालतले सोही महाभियोग फाइल यसै वर्ष सेप्टेम्बर ९ मा टुंग्याएको थियो। त्यो पक्राउभन्दा दुई साताभन्दा केही बढी अघिको कुरा हो। तर यो पक्राउ महाभियोगसँग जोडिएको हो भनेर प्रहरी वा कुनै सञ्चारमाध्यमले जनाएको छैन।

संविधानको धारा २० अनुसार प्रहरीले उनलाई २४ घण्टाभित्र न्यायाधीशसामु पेस गर्नुपर्छ। सोमबारसम्म प्रहरीले उनलाई अदालत पुर्‍याउनुपर्छ, नत्र छाड्नुपर्छ।

सोमबारसम्म प्रहरीले जबराविरुद्धको उजुरी सार्वजनिक गर्ला, कि कारण नखोली उनलाई छाड्नुपर्ला?

────────────────────────

Former Chief Justice Cholendra Rana Arrested From Kathmandu Home, Complaint Undisclosed

A former Chief Justice was taken from his own home. Police still will not say why.

Police arrested former Chief Justice Cholendra Shumsher Rana from his Maharajgunj home overnight into Sunday, a senior police source told several outlets. A complaint was filed at the Kathmandu Valley Crime Investigation Office, Ratopati and Desh Sanchar reported, but its contents remain undisclosed.

In 2022, 98 lawmakers registered an impeachment motion against him citing 21 allegations of misconduct and corruption. Parliament never voted on it, and he retired in December 2022. On September 9 this year the Supreme Court's Constitutional Bench ruled the motion had lost its purpose. No outlet has reported any link between that ruling and the arrest.

Article 20 of the Constitution requires anyone arrested to be brought before a judge within 24 hours. By Monday, police must bring him before a judge or let him go.

By Monday, will police make the complaint public, or release him without ever saying why?
